bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang signals willingness to return; Veritas initiates Sell at $135; earnings tonight
bullets.body: Huang released first statement since resignation saying he'd be honored to return as CEO if the board decides it's in shareholders' best interest; prediction markets at 17% probability (up from 8%), behind ARM's Rene Haas at 20%. Board reportedly not considering reinstatement; Treasury Secretary Bessent pushing for external hire. Separately, Veritas Securities initiated Sell with $135 PT (12% downside vs ~$154); MS analyst cut FY28 growth forecast to +53% from +70% on regulatory headwinds. Buyside FY28 EPS estimates already down ~20% to ~$20; consensus expects NVDA to hold 70% FY27 growth guide tonight but 2028 fears won't be resolved by any single print.

bullets.title: NVDA/COHR/LITE/CIEN/MRVL: China optical transceiver ban advancing — optical names +3-8% premarket
bullets.body: Trump administration moving forward with initiative to ban Chinese optical transceivers; COHR and LITE up 8% and 5% pre-market, with ALAB, CIEN, MRVL, CRDO, FN, MTSI, GLW, VIAV all +3-7% in sympathy. One analyst cautions the rally is premature — any ban likely phased from 2029 and excludes legacy speeds. China represents two-thirds of the global optical market so the structural tailwind is real but timing is uncertain.

bullets.title: DIS: UBS upgrades to Buy; Q4 beats across the board, FY27 double-digit EPS growth reiterated
bullets.body: F4Q26 adj. EPS $1.77 beat consensus $1.67 on revenues of $25.95B vs. $25.16B; segment OI +43% y/y to $4.97B. Management reaffirmed double-digit FY27 adj. EPS growth ex-53rd week with ~$11B FCF, $9B buyback, and dividend raised to $2.00/share from $1.50. Domestic Parks OI +36%; Entertainment SVOD margins hit 13.6%. JPM reiterates Overweight; UBS upgrades to Buy; stock down ~2.5% premarket on DIS discontinuing SVOD OI disclosure and Asia parks pressure expected to persist into FY27.

bullets.title: HD: Q3 beat on comps/revenue; gross margin miss and CEO transition weigh; McPhail named CEO Nov 23
bullets.body: Q3 adj. EPS $3.86 beat $3.84; comps +2.2% vs. consensus +1.8%; revenue $43.4B beat $42.8B. FY27 revenue guidance raised to ~+4.5% but EPS growth held at +2% midpoint; gross margin 32.8% missed by ~20bps. CFO Richard McPhail named CEO replacing Ted Decker effective Nov 23. Street cites limited visibility into meaningful fundamental recovery but credits execution; premarket selling pressure expected from margin miss and implied Q4 comp deceleration.

bullets.title: HPE: FAA pauses router installation linked to nationwide ground stop — negative catalyst
bullets.body: Media reports that the FAA has paused installation of HPE routers tied to a nationwide ground stop; HPE stock was down $0.84 at time of alert. This is a reputational/operational negative ahead of HPE's upcoming earnings, where JPM buyside survey expects AI system orders/backlog of $3.39B/$7.93B and F27 revenue growth guidance of 13-17%.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE/CRDO/CIEN: JPM off-cycle hardware survey sets up high expectations into earnings
bullets.body: JPM buyside survey solicits expectations for DELL (~$49B F3Q27 revenue, AI server shipments ~$18.5B, $95B backlog), CRDO (>85% YoY growth, >$600M optical target), HPE (AI backlog $7.93B, 13-17% F27 revenue growth), and CIEN (>$10B year-end backlog). Survey seeks confirmation of management guidance raises across all names. JPM also hosting PC/server supply chain update call Nov 18 with read-throughs to DELL, HPE, and SMCI.

bullets.title: NOW: Agentic AI consumption up 13x y/y; non-seat revenue hits 50% of Q3; AI ACV raised to ~$1.7B
bullets.body: ServiceNow conference takeaways show agentic AI consumption up 13x year-over-year and non-seat-based revenue reaching 50% of Q3 revenue, a structural shift from traditional seat-based software. AI ACV expectations increased from initial $1B to ~$1.7B by Q3; Moveworks employee offering hit $100M in first three months with 60% y/y customer growth. Company gradually moving toward consumption-based pricing with commit-to-consume models.

bullets.title: MDB: MongoDB acquires Firebolt for real-time analytics capabilities
bullets.body: MongoDB announced acquisition of Firebolt, which provides real-time analytics on live operational data. Financial terms were not disclosed. The deal expands MongoDB's analytics capabilities alongside its core operational database platform.

bullets.title: MCHP: Raymond James reiterates Strong Buy but cuts PT to $80 from $125 on margin reset
bullets.body: December guidance of $1.606B came in below consensus of $1.627B; gross margin reset to 64-65% vs. prior ~66% expectations. Supply constraints are limiting shipments of higher-margin products and extending lead times to March/June. Positives: industrial revenue +50% y/y in September, data center +56%, book-to-bill above 1.0, net leverage improved to 2.36x from 2.85x, and 24 Gen6 PCIe design wins.

bullets.title: CVNA: Stifel initiates Buy at $85, adds to Core Four; loan performance mixed across vintages
bullets.body: Stifel initiates CVNA at Buy with $85 PT citing AI shopping potential and capacity advantages, adding to Core Four top picks. JPM loan data shows 2024 prime vintage tracking at 0.6x loss rate vs. 2023 (materially better) but 2025 vintage DQs tracking unfavorably at 1.2x vs. 2024. CVNA has not done a sub-prime ABS deal since Q1 2025. Overall credit remains stable with no meaningful shift in consumer health.

bullets.title: WSM: Stifel initiates Buy at $290; remains a consensus long at 80%+ crowding per Citi monitor
bullets.body: Stifel initiates WSM at Buy with $290 PT citing affluent customer base and B2B growth opportunity. Citi crowding monitor shows WSM at 80%+ long crowding but also saw the largest decrease in short crowding week-over-week, suggesting some positioning squeeze may have already occurred.

bullets.title: AMZN/DASH/CART: Amazon $7B India renewable energy commitment; DoorDash-Instacart merger faces DoJ review
bullets.body: Amazon announced $7B in renewable energy investments in India by 2030 (934 MW across three projects). Separately, the DoorDash and Instacart merger is facing DoJ antitrust review replacing FTC jurisdiction. Amazon and online channels continue to take share — non-store retailer sales accelerated to +11.8% adjusted y/y in October vs. +10.4% in September.

bullets.title: MSFT: Ignite keynote today; global outage traced to undetected July bug
bullets.body: CEO Satya Nadella keynotes Ignite today with focus on enterprise AI adoption, Copilot agents, and OpenAI partnership strategy; analysts expect no near-term guidance changes. The November global outage was caused by an undetected bug present since July — 80% of Outlook servers were unresponsive at peak and took 15 hours to identify and fix. MSFT outage alone estimated at $400M-$1.5B in insured cyber losses.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $500M geothermal PPA with Quaise Energy for Oregon data center power starting 2030
bullets.body: Google signed a power purchase agreement for 50 MW of superhot geothermal power from Quaise Energy's Project Obsidian in Central Oregon, valued at over $500M, with delivery beginning as early as 2030. The supply is intended for Google's data center operations in The Dalles, Oregon.

bullets.title: NFLX/BABA/FSLR/QBTS/RGTI hit 52-week lows; DIS at 52-week high
bullets.body: 191 stocks hit 52-week lows in the session. NFLX is down 45.4% YTD (low $60.70), BABA down 42.8% (low $88.00), FSLR down 37.3% (low $158.60), QBTS down 64.2% (low $8.40), RGTI down 65.6% (low $8.80). DIS bucked the trend at a 52-week high of $121.80 (+15.2% YTD) on earnings beat.

bullets.title: INTU: Preview in focus ahead of earnings; MSFT Ignite AI strategy a key read-through
bullets.body: MS TMT flags INTU as a name to watch with earnings preview in context of broader software sector — Ignite AI announcements from MSFT could inform competitive dynamics. No specific estimate changes cited but the note flags it alongside broader enterprise AI adoption themes.

bullets.title: META: Muse surpassed 10M DAUs in under 10 weeks; compute costs escalating with agent growth
bullets.body: META's Muse product surpassed 10M DAUs in under 10 weeks. Compute costs are escalating as agent-based product usage grows. Internet sector rated Attractive by MS with META up ~5% in the recent relief rally; trading at 22x 2026 EPS.

bullets.title: PLTR: Goldman hosting in-person product demo with CFO David Glazer tomorrow in NYC
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs is hosting a limited-attendance in-person PLTR product demo featuring CFO David Glazer and engineering leadership in New York on November 18. Goldman rates PLTR Buy; market cap ~$447.8B. No recording or transcription permitted.

bullets.title: SHOP: Down 1.9% in Canadian trading amid broader weakness
bullets.body: Shopify down 1.9% on the TSX amid broad market decline; S&P/TSX Composite down 0.55% in mid-morning trading. No company-specific catalyst cited.

bullets.title: DLB: Down 2.7% on 167% unusual volume ahead of earnings after close today
bullets.body: Dolby Laboratories trading down 2.7% on 167% unusual volume versus 30-day average with earnings expected after the close today. No specific news driving the unusual activity was immediately identified.
